question: Should health systems pay for new antibiotics by yearly subscription instead of by the dose sold?
answer: A good new antibiotic should sit unused until the old ones fail, so paying per dose rewards the opposite of good stewardship. England's pilot from 2022 paid up to £10 million a year per drug for ten years, whatever the volume. Only predictable income will bring investors back to a field where approval can still mean bankruptcy.
move: What decides it is whether guaranteed fees change what firms start to research.
counterpoint: Subscriptions pay for drugs that already exist; the shortage is in discovery, which a £10 million fee barely touches when one drug costs hundreds of millions to develop. One country's scheme is too small to steer global investment, and rewarding any approval invites tweaks of old classes rather than the genuinely new ones resistance demands.
